The study focuses on a two-bladed vertical axis wind turbine with a diameter of 1.7 m and NACA0015 aerofoil-profiled blades.
The selected test case corresponds to an optimum operating condition with a wind speed of 7 m/s and a tip speed ratio of 2.29.
The 2D computational domain is divided into four subdomains connected via non-conformal mesh interfaces, and the Sliding Mesh method is used to model the rotation of the turbine.
The baseline 2D mesh has 920,600 total elements with 1,000 nodes along each blade profile and a unity maximum dimensionless wall distance, y+.
The sensitivity of the averaged upstream torque coefficient to the change from the baseline domain to the extended domain is less than 1% for both turbulence models.
The solution is considered time-periodic at the 5th cycle for the SST k-ω model and the 6th cycle for the SST k-ω with γ transition model.
Increasing the temporal resolution from 540 to 1080 time steps per cycle results in less than 1% change in the averaged upstream torque coefficient for both turbulence models.
The results are most sensitive to the dimensionless wall distance, y+, with the SST k-ω with γ transition model being more sensitive to mesh attributes compared to the SST k-ω model.

The sensitivity of the averaged upstream torque coefficient to increasing the global refinement factor from 1.0 to 2.0 is about 1.07 and 0.19 for the SST k-ω and the SST k-ω with γ transition models, respectively.
The baseline 2D mesh is considered suitable for further analysis due to the trade-off between accuracy and computational cost.
The paper finds that the 2D results based on the SST k-ω with γ transition model deviate significantly from the detailed experimental data, while the trends change between the 2D and 3D cases.
The study compares the CFD predictions of pressure distribution around the blade and the pressure contribution to the instantaneous power coefficient against detailed experimental data.
The averaged Reynolds number based on the blade chord and the averaged theoretical relative velocity is about 2.5×10^5, which is in the transition flow regime.
The Sliding Mesh method is used in the 2D CFD model to account for the rotation of the turbine.
The solution is considered time-periodic at the 5th cycle for the SST k-ω model and the 6th cycle for the SST k-ω with γ transition model.
